learning_outcomes.text: Ability to develop radio communication systems: antenna design, equipment and subsystems, channel modeling, link calculation and planning.
Ability to design and manufacture integrated circuits.
Ability to design communication components such as routers, switches, concentrators, transmitters and receivers in different bands.
Ability to apply advanced knowledge of photonics and optoelectronics, as well as high-frequency electronics.
Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.

That students know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or little-known environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their area of study.
That students possess the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a way that will be largely self-directed or autonomous.

Ability for the commissioning, direction and management of electronic and telecommunications equipment manufacturing processes, guaranteeing safety for people and property, the final quality of products and their homologation.
Ability to apply acquired knowledge and solve problems in new or little-known environments within broader and multidisciplinary contexts, being able to integrate knowledge.
Possess skills for continuous, self-directed and autonomous learning.
Design antennas that meet the established requirements according to the frequency band using the appropriate technology and design methods.
Design and develop various passive subsystems for radiocommunications in different technologies and frequency bands.
Design and develop various active subsystems for radiocommunications in different technologies and frequency bands.
Use different topologies and design techniques to design and develop radiocommunication systems.
Design and integrate complex radiocommunication systems adapted to specific functionalities from passive and active subsystems in different technologies.
Adapt new design techniques and technologies to problems that require original and imaginative solutions by autonomously understanding them in a more global environment.
Solve non-canonical problems related to active and passive radiocommunication antennas and subsystems autonomously and self-directed.

syllabus_topics: Parameters and design tools for communication subsystems.
Specification and design of radio communication transmission and reception subsystems.
Design of planar antennas: microstrip and PIFA.
Design of aperture antennas: horns and reflectors.
Antennas based on periodic and quasi-periodic structures.
Implementation of filters in RF and microwave bands.
Spatial filters based on frequency selective surfaces.
Implementation of amplifiers in RF and microwave bands.
Implementation of mixers in RF and microwave bands.
Implementation of oscillators in RF and microwave bands.
Implementation in RF and microwave bands.
assessment_rules: For the theoretical block, a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required. The theoretical grade is calculated as 0.1 x ( T1 + (2 x T2) + T3 + T4 + T5 + T6 + (2 x T7) + T8 ). For the practical block, a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required. The practical grade is calculated as 1/30 x ( (2 x M) + PA ). If both minimums are met, the final grade is (0.7 x Theory) + (0.3 x Practicals); otherwise, the final grade is the numerical grade of the failed part. In extraordinary calls, the evaluation elements are the same, and if laboratory practices were completed in the ordinary call, that grade is retained.
